audioEnvelopeFallback.method: When no phoneme track exists, drive mouthOpen from the spoken audio's loudness envelope (RMS over 30 ms windows), smoothed with attack 40 ms / release 90 ms; pick width/round from the current word's first vowel in this database. Same method as the Juno Buddy 1.7 lip sync.

howItWorks: Speech text (or audio) is converted to a timed phoneme track.
Each phoneme maps to a viseme — a mouth shape — from the table below.
Viseme shapes are blended over time (coarticulation): the mouth starts moving toward the next shape before the current sound ends, which is what makes lip movement look smooth instead of choppy.
An expression layer (eyes, brows, smile) runs underneath the speech layer, and a motion layer adds blinks, gaze shifts, head nods and breathing.

Where phoneme timing is unavailable (browser speechSynthesis), fall back in order: (1) word-boundary events from the TTS engine, (2) a text-estimated track using average phoneme durations, (3) a loudness-envelope track from the spoken audio (the Juno Buddy 1.7 method).

integration.buildStep: QuestBuddi milestone: wire face-anim-db.json into app.js (fetch at boot, staged startup-checker step 'face database'), generate the viseme track in startSpeaking()/speakReply(), and retire the sine flap.
integration.currentState: app.js animates the mouth with a sine oscillation while speaking (mouth scale 1 + |sin(t*24)| * 0.85) and picks a static face expression per state. This database replaces the sine flap: the render loop should sample the active viseme track each frame and draw mouthOpen/mouthWidth/lipRound from here, layered over the active expression.
rendererTargets: 2D canvas face texture (current QuestBuddi face) — map mouthOpen/mouthWidth/lipRound/lipPress/teethShow/tongueShow directly onto the drawn mouth.
Future 3D head — the same 0..1 fields map 1:1 onto blendshape weights (jawOpen, mouthSmile, lipsPucker, lipsPress, etc.).

name: QuestBuddi Facial Animation Database
purpose: Drives the QuestBuddi companion's face so lips, jaw and expressions move smoothly with speech — the Meta-style live-avatar effect Cali directed us to build for our own AI companion. Replaces the old sine-wave mouth flap in app.js (mouth scale oscillating while speaking) with viseme-based lip sync, coarticulation smoothing, layered expressions, blinking and gaze.

timing.note: Blend toward the next viseme starting at 45% of the current phoneme's duration; ease with a smoothstep curve. Never snap. At phrase ends, release to sil over releaseMs.

visemes.label: f, v — lower lip to upper teeth
t, d, n, l — tongue tip up
k, g, ng — back of tongue
ch, j, sh, zh — lips pushed out
